categories.main_business_segments: Shikoku Electric Power Company operates five main business segments: Power Generation & Sales, Transmission & Distribution, Information & Communications, Energy (including LNG and related services), and Construction & Engineering. The group also engages in manufacturing of electrical equipment, trading, real estate, transportation, and various service businesses related to the electric power industry.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company relies on a diverse mix of power generation technologies, including nuclear (Ikata Nuclear Power Plant), thermal (coal, LNG, oil), hydroelectric, and renewable energy sources (solar, wind). It employs advanced grid management, high-efficiency power plant operations, digitalization of maintenance and operations, and is investing in technologies for decarbonization such as hydrogen, ammonia co-firing, and distributed energy resource integration.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Its primary customers are residential, commercial, and industrial electricity users in the Shikoku region, as well as wholesale electricity buyers across Japan. The company also serves telecommunications customers (individuals and businesses), LNG buyers, and clients in construction and engineering sectors.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s core operations are concentrated in the Shikoku region of Japan (Kagawa, Tokushima, Ehime, and Kochi prefectures), but it also has business activities and investments in other parts of Japan and overseas, including power generation projects in Australia and other international markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: Shikoku Electric Power operates across the entire electricity value chain: upstream (power generation), midstream (transmission and distribution), and downstream (retail sales to end-users). It also provides ancillary services such as telecommunications and engineering.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include ensuring stable energy supply, improving profitability through cost and revenue optimization, expanding growth businesses (especially renewables, international power generation, and ICT), and driving digital transformation (DX) and ESG initiatives. R&D focuses on cost reduction, asset longevity, digitalization, decarbonization, renewable energy integration, and new energy technologies such as hydrogen.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through electricity sales (retail and wholesale), transmission and distribution fees, telecommunications services, LNG sales, construction and engineering contracts, and various service and rental businesses. It also receives government subsidies for certain energy programs.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include other regional electric utilities in Japan (e.g., Kansai Electric, Chugoku Electric, Kyushu Electric), new power retailers, and independent power producers. Shikoku Electric is a mid-sized utility with a strong regional presence and is positioning itself as a multi-utility group with diversified services.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated sales were ¥851.4 billion, with net income attributable to shareholders of ¥68.3 billion. The company has recovered from losses in FY2022 and FY2023, showing strong profit growth in FY2024 and FY2025, with improving ROE (17.1%) and a solid balance sheet (total assets ¥1.69 trillion, equity ratio 26%).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Shikoku Electric Power emphasizes high-quality, reliable energy supply, comprehensive service offerings (energy, ICT, engineering), and a commitment to regional development and sustainability. Its differentiation lies in its integrated multi-utility model, strong local relationships, and proactive approach to decarbonization and digital transformation.
